body:
## Problem

#633 (PR #685) stops the run when a branch the fold already carried onto the line this run is rewritten. The check runs at the *next* fold. So a rewrite that lands during the run's last fold, or after it, is never caught by that run, and the line keeps a commit that is no longer on the PR branch. The up-front fetch the check adds also runs outside the integration lock. A ref-lock clash there stops the fold with "could not fetch". That fails closed, but it stops the run for a reason that has nothing to do with the bundles.

Both are listed in PR #685's "Known limits":

> the new up-front fetch runs outside the integration lock (fail-closed: a ref-lock clash stops the fold with "could not fetch"). A rewrite that lands *during* a fold is caught at the next fold, so one that lands during the run's last fold is not caught by that run.

## Evidence

eduralph/pdca-pdca `results/issue_633/pr-description.md:101-104`, signed off 2026-10-14.

## Possible fixes

1. Re-check every carried branch once more after the last fold (or at the end of the run), and report a rewrite as a hold or stop with the same message.
2. Take the integration lock for the up-front fetch, or retry once on a ref-lock clash before stopping.

## Done when

A carried branch rewritten during the last fold is reported by the run that folded it, and a ref-lock clash on the up-front fetch does not stop the run on the first try. Tests pin both.

Raised by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-14.
title: integrate: a carried branch rewritten during the run's last fold is not caught, and the up-front fetch runs outside the lock
